The test image shows corn plants with prominent yellow/white parallel stripes running along the length of the leaves, alternating with green tissue. Leaves appear somewhat narrow and erect. No brown spotting or lesions visible — the primary symptom is the bold striping pattern.

Top candidates:
- **Downy_mildew**: "white parallel stripes of varying width alternating with green tissue; infected leaves narrower than usual, erect"
- **Maize_streak_virus**: streaking patterns on leaves
- **Stewarts_wilt**: pale green to yellow streaks following leaf veins

The Downy mildew reference shows early seedling-stage symptoms (pale/yellow seedlings), but the test image shows more mature plants. However, the symptom description precisely matches what I see: **"white parallel stripes of varying width alternating with green tissue; infected leaves often narrower than usual, erect"** — which is exactly the pattern in the test image (bold parallel yellow-white stripes running the full leaf length, alternating with green tissue, on somewhat narrow erect leaves).

The other candidates don't fit as well:
- Stewarts wilt: streaks from flea beetle feeding scars, not uniform parallel bands
- Maize streak virus: narrower, finer streaks
- Maize dwarf mosaic: mosaic/mottle pattern, not parallel stripes
